en: The amihan brings cool, dry northeast winds to the Philippines between November and February.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is a perfect cone-shaped stratovolcano formed by layers of hardened lava and ash.
The marble stones used to carve statues in Angat, Bulacan, are metamorphic rocks formed from limestone.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features a full cave system where freshwater flows directly into the sea.
The Balatik, a local star pattern based on Orion, helps indigenous Filipino farmers track the changing seasons.
Diwata-1 is a microsatellite built by Filipino scientists to monitor weather patterns and forest cover from space.
The rich volcanic soil surrounding Mount Bulusan in Sorsogon provides essential nutrients for growing abaca plants.
The strong tides in Manila Bay during a full moon are caused by the aligned gravitational pull of the sun and moon.
The Valley Fault System in Luzon is a major geological fracture where tectonic plates grind past each other.
Typhoons forming over the warm Pacific Ocean gain energy from evaporated seawater before hitting the eastern Philippine coast.
Surigao del Norte produces large amounts of laterite nickel ore, which is mined to make stainless steel.
The Philippines experiences a tropical climate with distinct wet and dry seasons because it is located near the equator.
